newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse turnover plunges, prices lower.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse turnover plunges, prices lower.

text.p: Thin interest from retail investors, who dominate the Bucharest bourse, drove turnover and most share prices down on Thursday, pulling two independent indexes to year lows for the second time this week.
Volume was modest at 8,289 shares and turnover sank to 38.5 million lei, or half the previous session's level.
"The sentiment of anticipation is still in the air, investors are looking forward to pending new listings and seem no longer to want to buy much of anything else," said a trader.
Last week, the bourse said 11 companies had applied for listing but did not say when they would join in trading.

It also said public offers for 14 state companies -- including ONT Carpati SA national travel operator and the only local newsprint maker Letea SA -- would be held through the exchange, where they would be subsequently traded.
The stock exchange now trades 13 of 16 listed stocks.
Thursday's thin buying focused on fertiliser maker Azomures SA and Artrom SA ARTM.BX engineering company.
Azomures took over 50 percent of total turnover and closed 100 lei stronger at 9,850. Artrom traded 4,279 shares, or half the total shares changing hands. It marked time at 2,000 lei.
The unofficial VAB and BIG value-weighted indexes of all listed stocks, computed by Vanguard SA securities and Bucharest Investment Group respectively, touched year lows.
The VAB was 1.5 percent down from the previous session to 291.7 points and the BIG dropped 1.6 percent to 289.98 points. Their base was 1,000 points when they started being computed last November.
Prices are on MRRO and MRRP.
